children.text: Newborn: judge the INR against neonatal ranges from the same lab — vitamin K-dependent factors start near half of adult levels (Andrew 1987).
Difficult draw, underfilled citrate tube or sample from a heparinized line: redraw by clean venipuncture.
INR differs between labs on the same blood. Record the lab with the number and trend within one lab.
On warfarin or another vitamin K antagonist: not this card — follow the anticoagulation plan.

children.subtext: No further workup; repeat if it was found for a reason

children.cond: Active or intracranial bleeding — in an infant also vomiting, bulging fontanelle, seizures, lethargy

pill.text: Emergency department / PICU now: IV vitamin K; urgent head imaging in an infant; PCC or plasma for life-threatening bleeding
Think HSV and sepsis: start IV acyclovir and antibiotics now; PICU; call hepatology

children.cond: Encephalopathy, hypoglycemia, jaundice with ALT in the thousands

pill.text: Treat as acute liver failure: give parenteral vitamin K and call hepatology / transplant center now — do not wait for the recheck

children.cond: Sepsis or shock, low platelets or falling fibrinogen

pill.text: Think DIC: PICU; treat the cause

children.cond: Young infant: INR out of proportion to the bilirubin

pill.text: Admit: think tyrosinemia (succinylacetone), galactosemia (stop lactose; send GALT before any red-cell transfusion), GALD; parenteral vitamin K; hepatology today

children.text: Before the dose, send factors V, VII, VIII and fibrinogen (and PIVKA-II where available) — factor VII changes within hours of vitamin K.
Give vitamin K IV or subcutaneously, not by mouth: 1–10 mg (Mouzaki 2019). Limited infant dosing data — confirm the dose with pharmacy. IV reactions, including anaphylaxis, are reported.
INR > 1.5, or any infant: call hepatology today while you give vitamin K.
Recheck the INR the next day.
Vitamin K deficiency, not synthetic failure.

pill.text: Fractionated bilirubin and stool color today; call hepatology — vitamin K deficiency can be the first sign of biliary atresia

children.cond: Cystic fibrosis, malabsorption, antibiotics, poor intake

pill.text: Daily vitamin K 2–5 mg (Mouzaki 2019); INR every visit and before procedures
Direct bilirubin, GGT; look for cholestasis or fat malabsorption; hepatology clinic
Meets the PALF coagulopathy criterion: call hepatology / transplant center now

children.cond: Factors V and VIII both low, fibrinogen falling
Factor V low, factor VIII normal or high

pill.text: Synthetic failure: hepatology today; watch glucose and mental status

children.cond: Factor V normal, INR < 2.0 without encephalopathy

pill.text: Mostly deficiency: repeat parenteral vitamin K and recheck INR (expert opinion); hepatology today

children.text: Order factors V, VII and VIII together: the pattern, not one level, gives the answer (Tripodi 2011; Pereira 1992).
The INR does not predict procedural bleeding (Intagliata 2023). Do not give plasma to correct the number.
Check platelets and fibrinogen; treat infection and kidney injury first.
Liver biopsy: ESPGHAN still asks for correction or a transjugular or laparoscopic route above INR 1.5 — agree the plan with the proceduralist.
